editorial:
Set in 17th-century Amsterdam, this drama follows Sophia, a young woman married to a wealthy older man, who falls for Jan, the artist painting her portrait. Their secret affair grows as they gamble on the wild tulip market, hoping one big win can buy them a new life. The movie has a lush, old-world feel, with candlelit rooms, fancy clothes, and tense choices that keep you watching. It is more slow and moody than action-packed, so expect romance, secrets, and bad decisions rather than big thrills.

The acting is strong, especially from the leads, and the costumes and sets look rich. Some scenes feel slow, and the plot can get confusing with side characters and tulip deals. Still, if you like period romance with betrayal and high stakes, it is worth a look. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or buy the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Sophia passes Maria's baby off as her own, and Cornelis believes he has a child. Sophia and Jan plan to escape, but Jan is robbed of the tulip bulb and money, so he misses their boat. Sophia sails away thinking he left her, while Cornelis raises the baby. Jan is left behind, and the lovers never get their planned future together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves period romance, secret affairs, and dramatic twists.
